newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee power plant seen back up next week.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee power plant seen back up next week.

text.p: The 910 megawatt (MW) Maine Yankee nuclear power plant is likely to resume power generation sometime next week, its operator said Friday.
"The Maine Yankee nuclear power plant expects to go back on line next week after a complete review of cable systems," the operator said in a statement.
The plant was shut December 6 after engineers found a couple of cables to the plant's main control room had been improperly routed.
The operators on Thursday gave a tentative restart date of "over the weekend."
Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities and 22 percent by other New England utilities.

Forecasters said Friday a storm is likely to move through New England this weekend, bringing either rain or wet snow to the area. A similar storm last weekend knocked out power to about 160,000 customers.
Northeast Utilities said yesterday it had restored power to nearly all of its customers in Connecticut, New Hampshire and western Massachusetts.
